finding: Novel tier proteins have zero BLAST homology in nr at any e-value
interpretation: Genuinely novel dark matter proteins (classifier confidence 0.85-0.99) have no detectable sequence homology in NCBI nr at e-value=10, confirming they represent true biological dark matter with no known relatives. The ESM-2 MLP classifier functionally annotates these proteins despite the complete absence of sequence homology — something BLAST cannot do. This validates the two-tier confidence stratification: high-confidence predictions (>0.99) are near-relatives of known proteins (95.6% BLAST hit rate), while moderate-confidence predictions (0.85-0.99) are genuinely novel with no known relatives (0% BLAST hit rate).
yancopoulos_one_sentence: ESM-2 protein language model embeddings functionally annotate Red Sea bacteriophage proteins that have zero sequence homology in the entire NCBI database — annotating the truly unknown for the first time.
